heading: Our values in practice
text: The five values (Own it, Say it plainly, Keep the customer in the room, Build to last, Grow people on purpose) are the test for any situation this policy does not cover. If in doubt, ask your manager or the HR Business Partner before acting.

heading: Respectful workplace
text: - Treat colleagues, customers and partners with courtesy. Bullying, abusive language, discrimination on any ground and retaliation for raising a concern are not tolerated. - Sexual harassment is handled under the Prevention of Sexual Harassment Policy (ZEN-POL-008) and the Internal Committee, not by line managers. - Zenvora is an equal-opportunity employer. Hiring, pay, promotion and exits are decided on merit and role requirements.

heading: Conflict of interest
text: Declare any situation where a personal interest could affect, or appear to affect, your judgement at work. Declarations go to the Head of People & Culture through ZenPeople.  - Hiring, managing or influencing the pay of a close relative requires written disclosure and a different decision-maker. - Financial interests above 1 percent in a customer, supplier or competitor must be declared. - Board seats or advisory roles outside Zenvora need written approval of the department head and the Head of People & Culture.

heading: Moonlighting and outside work
text: Employees may not take paid or unpaid work, consulting or freelance projects outside Zenvora unless approved in writing by their department head and the Head of People & Culture.  - Approval is never given for work that competes with Zenvora, uses its confidential information or equipment, or affects availability during working hours. - Unapproved moonlighting is treated as a serious conduct issue under the Progressive Discipline Policy (ZEN-POL-004). - Open-source contributions and teaching on personal time are allowed without approval if no confidential material is used.

heading: Gifts, hospitality and anti-bribery
text: - Never offer, promise or accept a bribe or improper payment, directly or through a third party, to or from any public official or private party. - Gifts or hospitality worth more than INR 3,000 per giver per year must be declared to HR within 7 days of receipt. HR may ask you to return or donate the gift. - Client entertainment follows the limits in the Travel & Expense Reimbursement Policy (ZEN-DPL-FIN-01).

heading: Confidential information and intellectual property
text: Customer data, source code, pricing, financials and unreleased plans are confidential. Handle them under the Information Security Policy (ZEN-POL-006). Work created in the course of employment belongs to Zenvora. Your confidentiality duty continues after you leave.

heading: Raising concerns (whistleblower channel)
text: Report suspected violations to your manager, the HR Business Partner, or confidentially to ethics@zenvora.example. Concerns about the CEO or senior leaders can be sent directly to Dr. Anjali Mehra, independent director and chair of the Audit Committee. Retaliation against anyone who raises a concern in good faith is itself a serious violation.

heading: Consequences
text: Breaches of this Code are handled under the Progressive Discipline Policy (ZEN-POL-004). Fraud, bribery, theft and harassment are not subject to progressive steps and may lead to immediate termination.

heading: Standard rule: three days in office
text: - Every employee works from the office (WFO) at least 3 days per week, as set in the team roster. - Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday are the anchor days. Teams plan shared meetings, design reviews and demos on these days. - Monday and Friday are flexible. Remote days are worked from home (WFH) or from a client site. - Client visits and business travel count as WFO days.

heading: Who must work from office on all working days
text: The following groups work from office on every working day, without exemption, until the condition ends:  - Trainees and interns in band Z1. - New joiners in the first 90 calendar days after the date of joining (induction). - Employees serving a notice period after resignation or termination. - Employees not allocated to any project or work stream for more than 10 working days. - Customer Support employees on the Care Centre shift roster (see ZEN-DPL-CSC-01).

heading: Rosters and deviations
text: - The reporting manager designs the team roster and publishes it in ZenPeople at the start of each month. - Any deviation from the roster must be approved in advance by the department head. - Employees may work from home 'anywhere in India' for up to 12 days per financial year with department head approval. Working from another country needs written approval from the Head of People & Culture and the CFO because of tax and legal exposure.

heading: Attendance and working hours
text: - Normal working time is 9 hours a day. Core hours are 10:30 to 16:30 IST, when everyone should be reachable. - In office, attendance is recorded by the door access card (first entry and last exit). - On remote days, employees clock in and out in ZenPeople. Attendance is validated against timesheets and leave records. - Two unapproved roster deviations in a calendar month lead to a conversation with the manager and HR Business Partner (Phase 1 of ZEN-POL-004).

heading: Sickness and leave
text: An employee who falls ill on a WFO or WFH day should apply for Sick Leave under the Leave Policy (ZEN-POL-003) rather than work unwell.

heading: Working from home standards
text: - Follow the Code of Conduct (ZEN-POL-001) and dress code norms during video meetings. - Follow the Acceptable Use Policy (ZEN-POL-005) and Information Security Policy (ZEN-POL-006): use only company laptops, no public Wi-Fi for Restricted data, lock your screen. - A home internet allowance of INR 1,000 per month is paid to employees in hybrid mode on request through ZenPeople Expenses.

heading: Meeting etiquette
text: - Cameras on in team meetings on remote days. Start and end on time. - Focus Friday: no internal meetings before 12:00 on Fridays unless urgent. - Share an agenda in the invite. Write down decisions and owners in Confluence or Slack the same day.

heading: Austin Regional Supplement
text: Employees based at the Austin sales office are remote-first. They meet customers in person where useful, use the Austin co-working space as needed, and follow the US public holiday calendar. All other parts of this policy and of the Code of Conduct, Acceptable Use and Information Security policies apply, subject to local law.

heading: Compliance
text: Regardless of work mode, every employee must follow all Zenvora policies, including the Leave Policy, Code of Conduct, Acceptable Use Policy and Information Security Policy. Failure may lead to action under the Progressive Discipline Policy (ZEN-POL-004).

heading: How to apply
text: - Apply in ZenPeople. For planned leave of more than 2 days, apply at least 3 working days ahead. - In case of sickness, inform the manager by 10:30 IST on the first day and apply in ZenPeople on return. - Unapproved absence of 3 or more days in a row is treated as absconding and handled under the Progressive Discipline Policy (ZEN-POL-004).

heading: Probation and notice period
text: - New joiners are on probation for 6 months. EL can be availed only after probation is confirmed. - Notice period after probation is 60 days for bands Z1 to Z3, 90 days for Z4 to Z6, and 120 days for Z7 and Z8. During probation it is 30 days. - Leave may not be used to shorten a notice period unless the manager and the Head of People & Culture agree in writing. Employees serving notice work from office on all working days (ZEN-POL-002).

heading: EL encashment and carry forward
text: At the end of the financial year, EL above a balance of 30 days is encashed with the April payroll. On exit, the remaining EL balance is encashed at basic pay divided by 26 per day. CL and SL are not encashed.

heading: Sabbatical
text: Employees with at least 5 years of service may take up to 4 weeks of unpaid sabbatical once, with the approval of the department head and the Head of People & Culture. Benefits continue during the sabbatical.

heading: Leave during maternity, paternity and long absence
text: Employees on maternity leave continue to receive group health insurance. Their performance is rated pro-rata and the absence is not held against them in appraisals (see ZEN-DPL-HR-01).

heading: Principles
text: Discipline is meant to correct behaviour, not to punish. Zenvora may combine or skip steps depending on the facts and the seriousness of the issue. Factors considered include whether the issue repeats after coaching, the person's work record and the impact on customers, colleagues and the company.

heading: Phase 1: Verbal warning
text: The immediate manager meets the employee together with the HR Business Partner. They explain the issue or policy breach, the expected standard and the steps needed to improve. The meeting is noted in ZenPeople.

heading: Phase 2: Written warning and Performance Improvement Plan
text: The immediate manager and the department head meet the employee with the HR Business Partner present. The incidents, earlier conversations and consequences of continued failure are documented in a written warning.  A formal Performance Improvement Plan (PIP) is issued within 5 business days of the Phase 2 meeting. A PIP runs for 30 to 60 days with clear goals and weekly check-ins.

heading: Phase 3: Suspension and final written warning
text: Used when temporary removal from work is the most effective action. The immediate manager may suspend an employee with pay pending an investigation when safety or evidence is at risk (up to 15 working days). Suspension as part of normal progression needs approval from the department head and the Head of People & Culture. Suspension without pay needs the CEO's approval and is limited to full-day increments. Pay is restored in full if the investigation clears the employee.

heading: Phase 4: Recommendation for termination
text: The department head may recommend termination. The recommendation needs approval from the Head of People & Culture. For employees in band Z5 and above, the CEO gives the final approval. Termination may happen without earlier phases for serious misconduct.

heading: Issues not subject to progressive discipline
text: The following can lead to immediate suspension or termination, without earlier steps:  - Sexual harassment (investigated by the Internal Committee under ZEN-POL-008). - Theft, fraud, bribery or falsification of records, credentials or expense claims. - Violence, threats or fighting at work. - Working under the influence of alcohol or drugs. - Intentional breach of data security or deliberate misuse of customer data (ZEN-POL-006). - Illegal behaviour, which may also be reported to the police.

heading: Appeals
text: The employee may submit information that challenges the facts used in the disciplinary action, or explains extenuating circumstances. This can be done at the meeting or within 5 business days after it, in writing to the Head of People & Culture. The Head of People & Culture reviews with the department head and decides within 10 business days. A final appeal can be made to the CEO.

heading: Documentation
text: The employee receives copies of all discipline documents, including any PIP, and signs to acknowledge receipt and understanding. Copies are kept in the employee's personnel file in ZenPeople.

heading: Company email
text: - Every employee gets an email address in the form name.surname@zenvora.example. It is for company business only. - Formal email includes customer agreements, official documents, reports and letters to applicants. Personal email (friends, family, shopping) must not be used for company business. - Never use a customer's email address for internal communication. - Access to company email is a privilege and can be restricted without notice if needed to protect the company.

heading: Chat and collaboration tools
text: Use Slack for internal chat, Confluence for documentation and Jira for work tracking. Do not move customer data into personal chat apps. Customers are contacted only through Pulse business numbers and company email.

heading: Internet use
text: Internet access is provided for work. Brief personal use is fine if it does not affect work or security. Sites with offensive, violent, sexually explicit or illegal content are blocked and must not be accessed on company devices.

heading: AI tools
text: - Use only AI tools on the approved list maintained by IT & Security and Data & AI. - Never paste Confidential or Restricted data (customer conversations, source code of Pulse core, personal data, financials) into any AI tool that is not approved for that data class. - You are responsible for checking AI-generated code, text and numbers before using them.

heading: Personal devices
text: Personal phones may be used for Okta, email and Slack only if enrolled in mobile device management (MDM). Personal laptops are not allowed for company work.

heading: Social media
text: Do not speak for Zenvora on social media unless authorised by Marketing. Never post customer information, screenshots of internal tools or unreleased plans.

heading: Monitoring and audits
text: Zenvora may monitor and log use of its systems, including sites visited, downloads, email and chat on company accounts, to protect security and comply with law. IT & Security audits systems periodically for abuse or misuse.

heading: Consequences of misuse
text: Abuse or misuse of company technology leads to warnings or disciplinary action under the Progressive Discipline Policy (ZEN-POL-004), up to and including termination. Deliberate data theft or access to illegal content may lead to immediate termination.

heading: Data classification
text: | Class | Examples | Handling | |---|---|---| | Public | Website content, published blogs | No restriction. | | Internal | Policies, org charts, internal wiki | Company people only. | | Confidential | Product roadmaps, financials, contracts, source code | Need-to-know. Encrypted in transit and at rest. | | Restricted | Customer conversations, personal data, credentials, keys | Named access only, masked in analytics, never in unapproved tools. |

heading: Accounts and devices
text: - Sign in through Okta with multi-factor authentication. Passphrases must have at least 14 characters. Never share accounts. - Company laptops are encrypted and managed (MDM). USB storage is blocked by default. - Lock your screen when away. Do not leave Restricted data on screens in public places.

heading: Reporting incidents
text: Report any suspected security incident (lost device, phishing click, wrong-recipient email, suspected breach) within 1 hour of discovery to security@zenvora.example or in Slack #incidents.  - The CISO classifies the incident and leads the response with DevOps & Cloud. - Where legally required, the CISO reports incidents to CERT-In within 6 hours of becoming aware. - Customers are notified as required by their contracts, normally within 72 hours of confirmation.

heading: Access management
text: Access follows least privilege and is reviewed every quarter. Leavers lose access within 4 hours of their last working hour (see ZEN-DPL-ITS-01).

heading: Training
text: Every new joiner completes security awareness training within 30 days of joining. Everyone repeats it annually and takes part in quarterly phishing simulations.

heading: Third parties
text: Suppliers who handle Confidential or Restricted data need a security review and a signed data processing agreement before access is granted.

heading: Physical security
text: Visitors sign in and are escorted. Access cards are personal. Report lost cards the same day.

heading: Non-compliance
text: Violations are handled under the Progressive Discipline Policy (ZEN-POL-004). Intentional breaches are not subject to progressive steps.

heading: Our commitments
text: - Comply with applicable health, safety and environmental laws and standards. - Identify hazards, reduce risks and learn from incidents and near misses. - Train employees and involve them in keeping workplaces safe. - Reduce energy and paper use and promote sustainable practices.

heading: Emergency readiness
text: - Fire drills are held twice a year (April and October) at every location. - Floor wardens are named for each floor. There are certified first-aiders at each location: 4 in Hyderabad, 2 in Bengaluru and 3 in Visakhapatnam. - Emergency numbers and assembly points are displayed at every entrance.

heading: Reporting incidents and near misses
text: Report any injury, incident, near miss or unsafe condition within 24 hours using the EHS form in ZenPeople or ehs@zenvora.example. Reporting a near miss is encouraged and never penalised.

heading: Night-shift and commute safety
text: Employees whose shift ends between 20:00 and 06:00 get company cab transport, with GPS-tracked vehicles and a security escort for women employees on night routes. This applies to the Care Centre roster (ZEN-DPL-CSC-01).

heading: Ergonomics and wellbeing
text: - A desk and chair assessment is offered to every employee at joining and for hybrid work set-ups on request. - Take short breaks from screens. An annual health check-up and group health insurance are provided. - A confidential Employee Assistance Programme (EAP) offers free counselling 24x7.

heading: Employee responsibilities
text: - Follow safe work procedures, signs and instructions. - Report injuries, incidents and near misses promptly. - Take part in drills and training.

heading: What counts as sexual harassment
text: - Unwelcome physical contact or advances, requests for sexual favours, sexually coloured remarks, showing pornography, or any other unwelcome physical, verbal or non-verbal conduct of a sexual nature. - Conduct in person, by message, email, chat, calls or on social media, at the office, at client sites, on work travel, at events, or on remote days.

heading: How to complain
text: 1. Submit a written complaint to the Presiding Officer within 3 months of the incident (or the last incident). The IC may extend this by a further 3 months for good reason. The IC will help you put the complaint in writing if needed. 2. The IC may arrange conciliation if the complainant requests it. No monetary settlement is used as the basis of conciliation. 3. If there is an inquiry, the IC completes it within 90 days, gives both parties a fair hearing and submits its report within 10 days of completion. 4. Zenvora acts on the recommendations within 60 days, using the Progressive Discipline Policy.

heading: Interim relief
text: During an inquiry the IC may recommend interim measures such as a change of reporting line or seat, or up to 3 months of leave for the complainant.

heading: Confidentiality and non-retaliation
text: The identity of the people involved, the complaint and the inquiry are confidential. Anyone who retaliates against a complainant or witness faces disciplinary action. A knowingly false complaint is also a conduct violation.

heading: Awareness and reporting
text: All employees complete POSH awareness training within 30 days of joining and annually after that. The IC files an annual report as required by law.

heading: Cycle
text: The financial year runs from 1 April to 31 March. There are two half-yearly cycles: H1 (April to September, reviewed in October) and H2 (October to March, reviewed in April). Salary revisions take effect on 1 April, based on the H2 review. Promotions are considered in April, with exceptional off-cycle promotions possible in October.

heading: Goals
text: Within 3 weeks of the start of each cycle, every employee agrees 3 to 5 OKRs (objectives and key results) with the manager in ZenPeople. Goals are reviewed at monthly one-to-ones.

heading: Ratings
text: | Rating | Meaning | |---|---| | 1 | Needs improvement | | 2 | Partially meets expectations | | 3 | Meets expectations | | 4 | Exceeds expectations | | 5 | Outstanding |  No more than 10 percent of a department may be rated 5 in a cycle.

heading: Calibration
text: After manager reviews, the department head and the HR Business Partner calibrate ratings across the department to keep standards consistent. Ratings are shared with employees only after calibration.

heading: H1 FY2026-27 calendar
text: | Step | Dates | |---|---| | Self-review window | 5 October to 16 October 2026 | | Manager reviews | 19 October to 30 October 2026 | | Calibration | 2 November to 6 November 2026 | | Feedback conversations | 9 November to 20 November 2026 | | Results visible in ZenPeople | By 27 November 2026 |

heading: Rating of 1 or 2 and PIP
text: An employee rated 1, or rated 2 in two consecutive cycles, is placed on a Performance Improvement Plan under Phase 2 of the Progressive Discipline Policy (ZEN-POL-004).

heading: Special situations
text: - Employees on maternity or other long leave are rated pro-rata on the period worked and are not penalised for the absence (ZEN-POL-003). - Employees serving notice are not eligible for increments or promotion. - New joiners with less than 3 months in the cycle are reviewed in the next cycle.

heading: Transport
text: - Flights: economy class. Band Z6 and above may use premium economy on flights longer than 5 hours. - Train: AC 3-tier for Z1 to Z4, AC 2-tier for Z5 and above. - Local travel: ride-hailing or auto. Own vehicle: INR 8 per km for a car and INR 3.5 per km for a two-wheeler.

heading: Daily allowance
text: Domestic food allowance is INR 1,200 per day for Z1 to Z4 and INR 1,500 per day for Z5 and above. International per diem is USD 75 for Z1 to Z5 and USD 100 for Z6 and above.

heading: Claims
text: - Submit within 30 days of the end of the trip in ZenPeople Expenses with receipts for every item above INR 500. - Finance settles approved claims within 10 working days. Advances up to 80 percent of the estimate are available. - Client entertainment needs prior approval and is capped at INR 2,500 per head.

heading: Not reimbursed
text: - Alcohol, fines, personal entertainment, class upgrades paid by choice, and expenses without receipts above the limit. - False claims are a serious conduct issue under the Code of Conduct (ZEN-POL-001) and the Progressive Discipline Policy (ZEN-POL-004).

heading: Languages and stack
text: Approved languages are Go and Python (FastAPI). Any other language or datastore needs an Architecture Decision Record (ADR) approved by the Principal Backend Engineer and the Director of Engineering.

heading: Branching and pull requests
text: - Trunk-based development with branches that live no longer than 2 days. - Pull requests should be under 400 changed lines where possible. - Every change needs CI to pass: build, tests, lint and security scan. - Review rule: 1 approval for most services. 2 approvals, including one Principal Engineer or Director, for services in the billing, payments and authentication paths.

heading: Quality bar
text: - New code must have at least 80 percent unit test coverage. - Public APIs are versioned. Deprecated public API versions get at least 6 months' notice. - Database migrations must be backward compatible (expand then contract). - Secrets live in AWS Secrets Manager, never in code.

heading: Service-level objectives
text: Every service defines SLOs. Defaults are 99.9 percent monthly availability and p95 latency under 250 ms. Services must expose metrics, logs and traces.

heading: Dependencies
text: Dependency updates are reviewed monthly. Critical vulnerabilities are patched within 7 days and high ones within 14 days.

heading: Ownership
text: Each service has a CODEOWNERS entry and a named on-call owner. Service owners join the on-call rota described in ZEN-DPL-DCL-01.

heading: Release trains
text: - Web: release every second Tuesday. - Mobile: monthly release train on the first Tuesday of each month. - Mobile rollouts are staged: 5 percent, then 25 percent, then 100 percent, with a 24-hour hold between steps. Halt the rollout if crash-free sessions fall below 99.0 percent.

heading: Accessibility
text: All new screens meet WCAG 2.1 level AA. Use Zenith Design System components first. An accessibility audit of the web app runs every quarter. The UX lead signs off design quality before release.

heading: Supported platforms
text: Web: the latest two versions of Chrome, Edge, Safari and Firefox. Mobile: Android 9 and above, iOS 15 and above.

heading: Performance budget
text: Largest Contentful Paint under 2.5 seconds. Initial JavaScript bundle at most 250 KB gzipped. Crash-free sessions at least 99.5 percent.

heading: Feature flags and signing
text: All user-facing changes ship behind feature flags. App signing keys are held by DevOps & Cloud in a secured vault and are never stored on personal laptops.

heading: Data handling
text: - Data classes follow the Information Security Policy (ZEN-POL-006). - Personal data in analytics tables is masked. Access is role-based and reviewed quarterly. - Customer conversation data is kept for the contract term plus 90 days, then deleted. Raw event logs are kept for 13 months. Aggregated analytics are kept for 5 years. - Data deletion requests are completed within 30 days.

heading: Release gate for AI features
text: Before any customer-facing AI feature ships, it must pass the golden-set evaluation run by QA:  - Accuracy of at least 92 percent. - Hallucination rate below 2 percent. - Zero failures on the red-team safety set.

heading: Human in the loop
text: AI replies about billing disputes, legal matters, health or safety must be reviewed by a human before being sent. Customers must be told when a reply is AI-assisted.

heading: Models and vendors
text: The approved model list is maintained by the Head of Data & AI with the CISO. Customer data is never used to train third-party models. Prompts and responses are logged with personal data masked and kept for 90 days.

heading: Incidents
text: Harmful, biased or confidently wrong AI behaviour in production is handled as at least a SEV2 incident under ZEN-DPL-DCL-01.

heading: Defect severity
text: | Severity | Meaning | |---|---| | P0 | Outage, data loss or security hole | | P1 | Major feature unusable, no workaround | | P2 | Feature degraded, workaround exists | | P3 | Minor or cosmetic |

heading: Release gate
text: - Zero open P0 or P1 defects. - No more than 3 open P2 defects, each with a written waiver from the QA Manager. - Regression suite pass rate of at least 98 percent. - At least 80 percent unit test coverage on new code. - Performance test: p95 latency under 300 ms at 2x peak load (k6). - No critical or high findings in the security scan.

heading: Sign-off
text: The QA Manager signs off every production release in Jira. Hotfixes need a smoke test and QA Manager approval within 2 hours.

heading: AI features
text: AI releases need the evaluation report from the golden-set harness (ZEN-DPL-DAI-01) attached to the release ticket.

heading: Test data
text: Test environments use synthetic or masked data only.

heading: Severity and response
text: | Severity | Meaning | Acknowledge within | Updates | |---|---|---|---| | SEV1 | Full customer-facing outage, data loss or security breach | 15 minutes | Every 30 minutes | | SEV2 | Major feature degraded | 30 minutes | Every hour | | SEV3 | Minor degradation | 4 hours | Daily | | SEV4 | Cosmetic or low impact | Next business day | As needed |

heading: Incident process
text: The primary on-call engineer acts as incident commander for SEV1 and SEV2 and opens a channel in Slack #incidents. A blameless post-mortem is published within 5 business days for SEV1 and SEV2.

heading: On-call
text: - Weekly rota with a primary and a secondary engineer. Handover is on Monday at 10:00 IST. - On-call allowance: INR 3,000 per week for primary and INR 1,500 for secondary. - An engineer paged for more than 1 hour between 22:00 and 06:00 gets a compensatory day off.

heading: Changes
text: Standard changes are pre-approved. Normal changes are reviewed in the change review on Tuesdays and Thursdays. Emergency changes need the incident commander's approval. There is a change freeze from 20 December to 2 January.

heading: Backup and recovery
text: Tier-1 services have an RPO of 15 minutes and an RTO of 4 hours. Disaster-recovery drills run twice a year, in May and November.

heading: Infrastructure rules
text: - All infrastructure is defined in Terraform. Console changes are not allowed except in emergencies. - Production access uses Okta and just-in-time elevation for 4 hours. - Every cloud resource must carry cost allocation tags for team and product.

heading: Stages
text: 1. Discover: customer research and problem definition. 2. Define: written product requirements document (PRD) with success metrics. 3. Design: concept and detailed design reviews with Engineering and QA. 4. Build: feature flags on, QA involved from the first sprint. 5. Launch: launch checklist completed. 6. Learn: review metrics 60 days after launch.

heading: Customer research
text: Every product manager holds at least 5 customer interviews per quarter. Customer participation requires consent.

heading: Launch checklist
text: - Documentation and help-centre articles ready. - Support training delivered at least 5 working days before launch. - Security and accessibility checks passed. - Marketing brief approved by the Marketing Manager. - Pricing approved if changed.

heading: Roadmap and sunsets
text: The roadmap is reviewed quarterly by the leadership team. Retiring a feature needs 6 months' notice to customers, and ending a beta needs 90 days. Pricing changes need the approval of the CEO, CRO and CFO.

heading: Discount approvals
text: | Discount on list price | Approver | |---|---| | Up to 10 percent | Account executive or business development manager | | Above 10 and up to 20 percent | Chief Revenue Officer | | Above 20 percent | CEO and CFO | | Contract term longer than 3 years | CEO |

heading: Contract authority
text: - Annual contract value up to INR 10 lakh: signed by the Chief Revenue Officer. - Annual contract value above INR 10 lakh: signed by the CEO. - Non-standard liability, data or exclusivity terms need legal review through the CFO, and security questionnaires need CISO review. - Payment terms longer than net 45 days need CFO approval.

heading: CRM discipline
text: Every opportunity is logged in HubSpot within 1 business day. Forecasts are updated every Monday.

heading: Outreach rules
text: India: respect the Do-Not-Disturb registry and give a clear opt-out. US: follow CAN-SPAM, include an unsubscribe link and a physical address in marketing email.

heading: Marketing claims
text: - Claims about performance or security must be backed by data or reports (for example ISO 27001 and SOC 2). - Customer logos and quotes need written consent. - Press statements are approved by the CEO. Social posts follow the Acceptable Use Policy (ZEN-POL-005).

heading: Shifts and rosters
text: | Shift | Hours (IST) | |---|---| | A (morning) | 06:00 to 15:00 | | B (general) | 13:00 to 22:00 | | C (night) | 21:00 to 06:00 |  - The Team Lead publishes the roster 7 days ahead. Everyone gets one weekly off. Shift swaps need Team Lead approval. - Night shift is voluntary and paid a night allowance of INR 300 per night. Cab transport applies to any shift ending between 20:00 and 06:00 (ZEN-POL-007). - Support staff work on site. Working from home is allowed only in a declared contingency such as a flood or transport strike.

heading: SLA targets

heading: Escalation
text: 1. Specialist works the ticket. 2. Escalate to the Team Lead when 50 percent of the SLA time has passed. 3. Escalate to the Head of Customer Care for any P1 or P2 SLA breach. 4. Engineering escalation goes through the on-call engineer (ZEN-DPL-DCL-01).

heading: Quality and targets
text: - CSAT target: 90 percent or above. First-contact resolution target: above 80 percent. - The Quality & Training Analyst audits 5 contacts per agent per week with a target score of 90 percent. - Call recordings are kept for 90 days.

heading: Overflow to partner BPO
text: When the queue exceeds 25 waiting contacts for more than 10 minutes, overflow goes to partner BPO Sutradhar Business Services. Partner agents see masked customer data only.

heading: AI assist
text: During the Sage pilot, agents review every AI-drafted reply before sending. Billing disputes, legal and health or safety topics must always be written or approved by a human (ZEN-DPL-DAI-01). Never take screenshots of customer data or keep personal notes about customers.

heading: Devices
text: - A laptop is issued on day 1 with accounts ready by 09:30. Laptops are refreshed after 3 years. - All devices are enrolled in MDM. Only software on the approved list may be installed. - Report a lost or stolen device within 2 hours to the helpdesk and security@zenvora.example. - Return devices within 3 working days of leaving. Disposal is certified.

heading: Access requests
text: Request access in Jira Service Management. Approval needs the manager and the system owner. Production access is just-in-time. Shared accounts are not allowed, and admin accounts are separate from daily accounts.

heading: Joiner, mover, leaver
text: - Joiner: access ready on day 1. - Mover: access re-checked within 5 working days of a role change. - Leaver: all access removed within 4 hours of the last working hour (immediately for involuntary exits).

heading: Access reviews
text: The CISO runs access reviews every quarter with system owners.
